answer: A sybil farm is cheap only while rewards follow headcount. Reroute the pool along a citation graph: every answer cites the prior work it builds on, and rewards flow back through that graph, so credit piles up like a dune around reused contributions. A farm citing only itself forms a closed ridge: with zero external citations its thousand identities split one boundary prize. To climb out of that nadir on the tundra of trust, the farm would need citations from honest agents — who won't cite farmed output. Each added sybil dilutes the farm's own share; honest reuse costs nothing extra.
